job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many students often believe that Fundamental Rights are absolute, meaning they can never be restricted under any circumstances. However, the Indian Constitution does not grant unlimited freedom. For instance, while you have the right to freedom of speech, you cannot use it to incite violence or threaten public order. The government can impose reasonable restrictions on your rights to maintain safety and harmony in society. Furthermore, the Right to Equality does not mean that everyone must be treated exactly the same regardless of their situation. Instead, it allows for special provisions, such as reservations, to uplift disadvantaged groups, ensuring true justice rather than just mechanical uniformity. If any of these rights are violated, the Right to Constitutional Remedies allows citizens to approach the courts for protection. This judicial safeguard ensures that rights are not just empty promises but are enforceable by law. Ultimately, rights are balanced against the needs of the community, ensuring that individual liberty does not harm the collective well-being of the nation.

items.evidence: For instance, while you have the right to freedom of speech, you cannot use it to incite violence or threaten public order.
items.q: Meena urges a crowd to attack a shop. What does the passage say about her speech?
options: Her speech can be stopped to keep public order
Her speech is protected, since rights are absolute
Her speech is protected, as free speech covers everything
Her speech can be stopped only by a court
items.explain: Free speech cannot be used to incite violence or threaten public order, so her speech can be restricted.

wrong.why: thinks Fundamental Rights can never be restricted
thinks free speech allows inciting violence
thinks only courts deal with rights, missing government's reasonable restrictions

items.evidence: The government can impose reasonable restrictions on your rights to maintain safety and harmony in society.
items.q: Why may the government place limits on people's Fundamental Rights?
options: To keep society safe and peaceful
To take rights away whenever it wishes
To make everyone earn the same income
To stop citizens from approaching the courts
items.explain: The government imposes reasonable restrictions only to maintain safety and harmony in society.

wrong.why: ignores the word 'reasonable' and thinks limits are unlimited
thinks rights aim at equal income for all
misses that citizens can always approach courts for protection

items.evidence: Instead, it allows for special provisions, such as reservations, to uplift disadvantaged groups, ensuring true justice rather than just mechanical uniformity.
items.q: Some say reservations break the Right to Equality. Which idea from the passage answers them?
options: Equality allows extra help for groups left behind
Equality means treating everyone exactly the same
Equality means everyone owns equal property
Equality can be restricted to keep public order
items.explain: Equality allows special provisions like reservations to uplift disadvantaged groups, giving true justice, not mechanical sameness.

wrong.why: thinks equality means identical treatment for all
picks a nearby passage idea that does not explain reservations

items.evidence: If any of these rights are violated, the Right to Constitutional Remedies allows citizens to approach the courts for protection.
items.q: An official violates Ravi's Fundamental Right. What can Ravi do?
options: He can ask the courts to protect it
He can only approach the Supreme Court
He can do nothing, as rights are promises
He can go to court only if society agrees
items.explain: The Right to Constitutional Remedies lets citizens approach the courts when any right is violated.

wrong.why: thinks only the Supreme Court can be approached
misses that rights are enforceable, not empty promises
misreads balancing with community needs as needing permission
